arrange.ko: 그녀가 어제 역 근처 서점에서 산 책은 매우 흥미로웠다.
arrange.bogi: was very interesting. / at the bookstore near the station yesterday / she bought / the book / that
arrange.ans: The book that she bought at the bookstore near the station yesterday was very interesting.

arrange.ko: 우리 마을 여름 축제에서 우리가 가장 즐긴 것은 강 위의 불꽃놀이였다.
arrange.bogi: was the fireworks show over the river. / what / most at the summer festival in our town / we enjoyed
arrange.ans: What we enjoyed most at the summer festival in our town was the fireworks show over the river.

arrange.ko: 그곳은 우리 가족이 매년 여름 사촌들과 함께 캠핑을 가는 조용한 호수이다.
arrange.bogi: where / the quiet lake / that is / goes camping with our cousins every summer / my family
arrange.ans: That is the quiet lake where my family goes camping with our cousins every summer.

arrange.ko: 그녀가 할머니의 오래된 정원에서 발견한 것은 우리 가족 모두를 기쁘게 했다.
arrange.bogi: pleased / she found in her grandmother’s old garden / everyone in our family. / what
arrange.ans: What she found in her grandmother’s old garden pleased everyone in our family.

arrange.ko: 그 가게는 연휴 동안 일찍 문을 닫았는데, 그것은 멀리서 온 많은 손님들을 실망시켰다.
arrange.bogi: disappointed / the store closed early during the holidays / many customers who had come from far away / , which
arrange.ans: The store closed early during the holidays, which disappointed many customers who had come from far away.

arrange.ko: 그 마을에는 지역 농부들이 주말마다 신선한 채소와 과일을 파는 큰 시장이 있다.
arrange.bogi: where / the town has / sell fresh vegetables and fruit every weekend / a large market / local farmers
arrange.ans: The town has a large market where local farmers sell fresh vegetables and fruit every weekend.

arrange.ko: 매일 30분씩 운동하는 사람들은 대개 그렇지 않은 사람들보다 더 건강하다.
arrange.bogi: are usually healthier than those who don’t. / people / who exercise for thirty minutes every day
arrange.ans: People who exercise for thirty minutes every day are usually healthier than those who don’t.

arrange.ko: 이것은 1890년으로 거슬러 올라가며 단순한 계산 실수에서 시작된 전설이다.
arrange.bogi: that / this is / dates back to 1890 / a legend / and started from a simple mistake in calculation.
arrange.ans: This is a legend that dates back to 1890 and started from a simple mistake in calculation.

arrange.ko: 구스타프 폰 붕게는 자신의 단순한 계산 실수로 시금치에 관한 통념을 만들어 낸 생리학자였다.
arrange.bogi: whose simple miscalculation / was / Gustav von Bunge / created a myth about spinach. / a physiologist
arrange.ans: Gustav von Bunge was a physiologist whose simple miscalculation created a myth about spinach.

arrange.ko: 우리는 공공장소에서 자유롭게 노는 아이들에 대한 관용을 되살려야 한다.
arrange.bogi: who / play freely in public spaces. / we need to / for children / build back our tolerance
arrange.ans: We need to build back our tolerance for children who play freely in public spaces.

arrange.ko: 곤충의 공격을 받은 미역취는 재빨리 주변 공기 중으로 화학 물질을 내보낸다.
arrange.bogi: that are attacked by insects / goldenrods / into the air around them. / quickly release chemicals
arrange.ans: Goldenrods that are attacked by insects quickly release chemicals into the air around them.

translate.en: What the monitoring system constantly checks is other people’s reactions to our behaviors.
translate.ko: 감시 시스템이 끊임없이 점검하는 것은 우리의 행동에 대한 다른 사람들의 반응이다.

translate.en: The technical term often used to describe animals’ judgement of numbers is the approximate number system.
translate.ko: 동물들의 수 판단을 설명하는 데 자주 사용되는 전문 용어는 ‘어림 수 짐작 능력’이다.

translate.en: Rhesus monkeys can tell one from two, two from three, three from four, four from five ... but start to fail from five upwards.
translate.ko: 붉은털원숭이는 1과 2, 2와 3, 3과 4, 4와 5는 구별할 수 있지만, 5부터는 실패하기 시작한다.

translate.en: Rats that learned to press a lever a given number of times, from four up to twenty-four, became markedly less and less precise in their responses as the number increased: by the top end of the range they would merely produce a spread of numbers around the target.
translate.ko: 네 번에서 스물네 번까지 주어진 횟수만큼 레버를 누르도록 학습한 쥐는 숫자가 커질수록 반응이 두드러지게 점점 덜 정확해졌다. 범위의 맨 위쪽에 이르면 그저 목표 수 주변에 흩어진 횟수를 내놓을 뿐이었다.

translate.en: It is a common observation that when testing the accuracy of animals’ number sense, the size of the numbers matters.
translate.ko: 동물의 수 감각의 정확성을 측정할 때, 숫자의 크기가 중요하다는 것은 흔히 관찰되는 사실이다.
